79341.subject: Can the AI arms race be stopped?
79341.body:
The Economist Picks

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/can-ai-arms-race-stopped-the-economist-akz2e?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BGO2d82l5Qvi36S2mB8ju8g%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3Sw5dA3bJD9Ys1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mu6zdj4q~eb-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mu6zdj4q-eb
  
Enjoying this newsletter? Get it in your inbox every Thursday, as well as our bonus weekend round-up of The Economist’s best journalism, by signing up for free here. When I was growing up, the most alarming technology was nuclear weapons. As a student, I lived with a family in Hiroshima who had been there when the bomb fell. As a young reporter, I interviewed many more eyewitnesses to the horror that ended the second world war. I even met a man, Yamaguchi Tsutomu, who had survived the blasts in both Hiroshima and Nagasaki.  Looking back, the nuclear age seemed more predictable than the present. Only a few governments had the bomb. The stand-off between the West and the Soviet Union was scary, but both sides had an existential reason not to start a nuclear war. People worried that a terrorist group might get its hands on a nuke, but they are hard to build. And there was never any question of the missiles developing minds of their own.  The geopolitics of AI are different. As the technology rapidly grows more potent, a worrying number of AI agents are escaping from their creators’ control. Boosters hope that AI will one day eliminate scarcity, but many in the industry fear there is a non-trivial chance it could eliminate humanity. Serious people, including the boss of Anthropic, are calling for a slowdown and stronger guardrails.  Yet, as our cover package describes, such wise caution clashes with power politics. America and China are in an AI arms race. Both governments believe that, as Donald Trump put it, the country that wins AI wins, so to slow down the development of frontier models would be to court defeat. President Trump says the only guardrail America needs is “a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT”, namely himself. It is not only Democrats who are sceptical of his approach; so are an increasing number of Republicans. As we argue, the future is fraught with danger (even if AI models are getting better at predicting it). Keeping the technology safe and keeping ahead of China are hard and contradictory goals. And for once, the journalistic cliché that “the stakes could not be higher” is actually true.   On The Insider this week, our editor-in-chief, Zanny Minton Beddoes, and colleagues report from Ukraine, where an AI-and-drones arms race is shaping the conflict—and offer a warning to Europe about what to expect in a world of rapid innovation

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin punched through $77,000 despite a Bank of Japan hike, but the bid underneath looks hollow — corporate treasuries have all but stopped buying and ETFs keep bleeding. 🏦 Bank of Japan Hikes to a 31-Year High — Bitcoin Tops $77,000 The BOJ raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to the highest level in 31 years. The yen weakened and, against every expectation of a risk-off reaction, bitcoin pushed above $77,000 in a third consecutive session of gains. Read full story 📉 Corporate Treasuries Bought Just 5,900 Bitcoin in Three Months Treasury company accumulation has collapsed to a trickle over the past quarter — the clearest sign yet that the corporate bid that carried the last cycle has gone quiet. Broader demand gauges look equally soft. More details 💸 Ether and XRP ETFs Post Outflows Even as Prices Climb Ether funds shed money for a third straight session while the token itself rose, and XRP products followed them out. Every major asset gained on the day, with zcash extending its run — a rally running on thin institutional fuel. See details ⚖️ SEC Grants Five-Year "Innovation Exemption" for Tokenized Securities The SEC issued a blanket five-year exemption allowing venues to list and trade tokenized securities without registering as a national exchange. It is the clearest U.S. pathway yet for real equities to move on-chain, with volumes, access and issuer rights kept under tight limits. Read more 🔓 Revolut Hackers Demand $3M in Monero, Threaten to Sell Customer Data A criminal group has put a 24-hour clock on Revolut, demanding 6,000 XMR — roughly $3 million — or it will sell hundreds of customers' identity documents and transaction records to other criminals, the Financial Times reported. Read full story ⚠️ Ethereum Locks In Glamsterdam Dates, Warns "Fake" Builders Could Stall the Chain Developers confirmed the upgrade schedule but flagged a live attack surface: free test ether lets fake builders outbid rivals and then withhold transaction payloads. Client teams get half the usual review time before the Sepolia run. More details ⚡ Solana Cuts Slot Time to 250ms — Blocks 17% Faster, Capacity Flat The network is trimming its target slot time, giving apps fresher on-chain data and shortening the window validators control. The trade-off: less work permitted per slot, so total transaction capacity stays where it was. Se
